Do you feel the vibration of a city that is growing too fast for its own skin? Do you feel the nervous electric energy of a place that is [music] reinventing what it means to be human? Welcome to New York City in the year 1880. We aren't just looking at old photographs [music] today through the lens of AI reconstruction based on the maps of Egbert Feler and the etchings of Harper's Weekly. We are stepping into the Gilded [music] Age at its most raw and roaring peak. I am [music] your guide and together we are going to walk the spine of Manhattan when it was the undisputed gateway to the new world. Our [music] journey today will take us from the very tip of the island where the world arrives in a frenzy of salt and steam up through the dark shadows of [music] the financial district and into the glittering chaotic heart of the city's social life. We will start at Castle Garden, move through the dense labyrinth [music] of lower Manhattan, cross the shadow of a bridge that isn't quite finished yet, and finish among the mansions that are pushing the city ever northward. New York in 1880 is a city of vertical dreams and horizontal squalor. A place where the richest men in history live blocks away from the most [music] desperate poverty on Earth. Let's begin where the story of modern America truly starts. [music] The water's edge. The sun is [music] just beginning to burn through the Atlantic fog. As we stand at the battery, look out at the harbor. It is a forest of masts. Steamships, their funnels belching [music] thick black soot. Jostel for space with elegant threemasted schooners. The air here is thick, tasting [music] of brine and the unwashed wool of a thousand coats. To our left is Castle Garden, a circular sandstone fortress that serves as the nation's primary immigrant depot. Before Ellis [music] Island ever opened its doors, this was the threshold. I can see a line of families, Irish, German, Italian, clutching wooden trunks and looking up at the skyline with a mix of terror and hope. This building was once a theater where Jenny Lind sang, but now it is a processing mill for human souls. Within a few decades, this fortress will be converted into the New York Aquarium, [music] and eventually the immigrants will be moved to the island in the distance, leaving [music] this place as a silent monument in a manicured park. We turn our backs to the sea and walk into the moore of Broadway. The transition is jarring. As we leave the open air of the battery, the buildings begin to lean over us. We are entering the financial [music] lungs of the world. Notice the ground beneath your feet. These aren't the smooth [music] streets, you know. These are Belgian blocks, rough rectangular stones slick with mud and horse manure. The sound is incredible. It is a constant grinding roar of iron rimmed wheels and the shouting of news boys. To our right rises the Trinity Church spire, which for now is the tallest point in the city. It seems impossible, but at this moment, [music] the church is the only thing reaching for God. The skyscrapers are still just blueprints in the minds of architects. This is the world of the old Nickerbachers, the elite families who are watching their quiet brownstone city be devoured by the relentless march of commerce. We push through the crowd, past men in silk top hats and messengers darting [music] between carriages. We are heading toward the intersection of Wall Street. Look at the telegraph [music] wires overhead. They are so thick they almost blot out the sun like a giant cobweb spinning the city together. Every shopfront here is a hive of activity. I see a group of bankers standing on the corner arguing over the price of Western railroads. There is a sense of immense unearned wealth being conjured out of thin air. But look down the side alleys, you'll see the sandwich men wearing boards advertising cheap meals for a nickel. This district will soon become a canyon of steel. And these telegraph wires will [music] be buried underground after the great blizzard of 1888. But for now, the chaos is all visible, tangled in the sky. [music] As we move north, the air changes. The smell of the docks fades, replaced by the scent of roasting coffee and the dry dust of construction. We are standing at the foot of Park Row, looking toward the East River. Towering above us is the most ambitious engineering project [music] in human history. The Brooklyn Bridge in 1880. [music] It is a ghost. The great granite towers are finished, rising like Gothic cathedrals from the water. But the roadway is not yet complete. I can see the delicate weblike steel cables stretched across the void. People call it the eighth wonder of the world. High above on the catwalks, workers, many suffering from the mysterious bends, are weaving the future of the city. >> Below the towers, the Fulton Fish Market is a riot of silver scales and shouting merchants. This bridge will link the two cities of New York and Brooklyn in just 3 years, changing the geography of power forever. But today, it is a haunting, beautiful skeleton [music] that dominates the horizon. We follow the curve of the island toward the east side and the atmosphere shifts violently. We are entering the fourth ward. The elegance of Broadway [music] is gone. The streets narrow and the buildings seem to groan under the weight of the people inside them. This is the world of the tenementss. Laundry hangs from every window like ragged flags. The smell here is overpowering. clogged sewers, rotting garbage, and the heavy scent of boiled cabbage and coal fire. I see children running barefoot through the slush, dodging heavy dreage wagons. This is the most densely populated [music] square mile on the planet. Families of 10 are squeezed into single rooms. It is a city of shadows where the sun rarely [music] touches the cobblestones. In a century, these slums will be cleared for high-rise housing and highways. [music] But today, this is the heartbeat of the city's labor. The engine room that keeps the mansions of the north [music] running. We escape the gloom of the tenementss and head west back toward the center of the island, rising up into Union Square. The contrast is like stepping into another world. The streets widen. The mud is replaced by swept pavement. We are in the Ladies Mile, the premier shopping district of the Gilded Age. Look at the shop windows of Tiffany and [music] Co. and Lord and Taylor. The women here wear elaborate silk dresses with bustles that sweep the ground, their faces shaded by parasol. The elevated railroad, the L, rumbles overhead on its iron stilts, casting rhythmic shadows over the street. [music] It is the sound of the future. I see a handsome cab pull up to the curb. A gentleman in a furlined coat stepping out to escort a lady into a [music] grand hotel. There is an air of indestructible confidence here. They believe this era of luxury will last forever. They cannot imagine that within a few generations, [music] these grand department stores will move even further up town, leaving these beautiful [music] cast iron buildings to be reclaimed by artists and lofts in a place [music] they will call Soho. [music] Finally, we walk north along Fifth Avenue toward the edge of the developing city. We stop near 50th [music] Street. To our left, the twin spires of the new St. Patrick's Cathedral have just been [music] completed, glowing white and pristine against the sky. But look around us. The city is still becoming. There are vacant lots filled with rocks and weeds. Shanty towns, huts made of scrap wood and tin sit right next to the rising marble palaces [music] of the Vanderbilts. We see the upper reaches of Central Park in the distance, a masterpiece of landscape that is still maturing. The air is cleaner here, smelling of fresh mortar and upturned earth. The Upper West Side is still largely goat farms and rocky outcrops. We are [music] standing at the frontier. The men building these mansions are the kings of the age, and they are carving their names into the very [music] rock of Manhattan. New York is a city built on the graves [music] of its previous selves. It never stops moving, never stops building, and never looks [music] back. But when we look at the reconstruction of 1880, we see the blueprint of the modern world. We see the same ambition, the same terrifying inequality, and the same desperate hunger for more that defines the [music] city today. The horses are gone and the telegraph wires have vanished, but the soul of the city, that electric, restless energy, remains unchanged. [music] Thank you for walking through time with me. If you could step into [music] any door in 1880 New York, where would you go? Would you brave the tenementss of the fourth ward, or would you take a seat at a gala in a Vanderbilt ballroom? segments.viText: Gia đình 10 người bị ép vào phòng đơn.

segments.text: It is a city of shadows where the sun rarely [music] touches the cobblestones.
segments.viText: Đó là thành phố của bóng tối nơi mặt trời hiếm khi [âm nhạc] chạm tới những viên đá cuội.

segments.text: In a century, these slums will be cleared for high-rise housing and highways.
segments.viText: Trong một thế kỷ nữa, những khu ổ chuột này sẽ được dọn sạch để xây dựng nhà ở cao tầng và đường cao tốc.

segments.text: [music] But today, this is the heartbeat of the city's labor.
segments.viText: [âm nhạc] Nhưng ngày nay, đây là nhịp đập lao động của thành phố.

segments.text: The engine room that keeps the mansions of the north [music] running.

segments.text: We escape the gloom of the tenementss and head west back toward the center

segments.text: The streets widen.
segments.viText: Đường phố mở rộng.

segments.text: The mud is replaced by swept pavement.
segments.viText: Bùn được thay thế bằng mặt đường quét.

segments.text: We are in the Ladies Mile, the premier shopping district of the Gilded Age.
segments.viText: Chúng tôi đang ở Ladies Mile, khu mua sắm hàng đầu của Thời đại Mạ vàng.

segments.text: Look at the shop windows of Tiffany and [music] Co.

segments.text: and Lord and Taylor.

segments.viText: Những người phụ nữ ở đây mặc những bộ váy lụa cầu kỳ với những vạt áo dài phủ kín mặt đất

segments.viText: những khuôn mặt được che bởi dù che nắng.

segments.viText: trên đường phố.

segments.text: [music] It is the sound of the future.

segments.text: I see a handsome cab pull up to the curb.
segments.viText: Tôi thấy một chiếc taxi đẹp trai tấp vào lề đường.

segments.text: [music] grand hotel.
segments.viText: [âm nhạc] khách sạn lớn.

segments.text: There is an air of indestructible confidence here.
segments.viText: Có một bầu không khí tự tin không thể phá hủy ở đây.

segments.text: They believe this era of luxury will last forever.
segments.viText: Họ tin rằng kỷ nguyên xa hoa này sẽ tồn tại mãi mãi.

segments.viText: tiến xa hơn nữa lên thị trấn, để lại những tòa nhà bằng gang [âm nhạc] tuyệt đẹp này

segments.viText: thành phố.

segments.text: To our left, the twin spires of the new St.

segments.text: But look around us.
segments.viText: Nhưng hãy nhìn xung quanh chúng ta.

segments.text: The city is still becoming.
segments.viText: Thành phố vẫn đang trở thành.

segments.viText: Có những bãi đất trống chứa đầy đá và cỏ dại.

segments.viText: Không khí ở đây trong lành hơn, có mùi vữa tươi và đất lật úp.

segments.viText: Upper West Side vẫn chủ yếu là các trang trại nuôi dê và các mỏm đá.

segments.text: We are [music] standing at the frontier.
segments.viText: Chúng tôi là [âm nhạc] đứng ở biên giới.

segments.text: The men building these mansions are the kings of the age, and they are
segments.viText: Những người xây dựng những dinh thự này là những vị vua của thời đại, và họ là

segments.text: carving their names into the very [music] rock of Manhattan.
segments.viText: khắc tên họ vào chính [âm nhạc] rock của Manhattan.

segments.text: New York is a city built on the graves [music] of its previous selves.
segments.viText: New York là một thành phố được xây dựng trên những ngôi mộ [âm nhạc] của chính nó trước đây.

segments.text: It never stops moving, never stops building, and never looks [music] back.
segments.viText: Nó không bao giờ ngừng chuyển động, không bao giờ ngừng xây dựng và không bao giờ nhìn lại [âm nhạc].

segments.text: But when we look at the reconstruction of 1880, we see the blueprint of
segments.viText: Nhưng khi nhìn vào quá trình tái thiết năm 1880, chúng ta thấy bản thiết kế của

segments.text: the modern world.
segments.viText: thế giới hiện đại.

segments.text: We see the same ambition, the same terrifying inequality, and the same desperate hunger
segments.viText: Chúng ta thấy cùng một tham vọng, cùng một sự bất bình đẳng đáng sợ và cùng một cơn đói khát tuyệt vọng

segments.text: for more that defines the [music] city today.
segments.viText: để biết thêm thông tin xác định thành phố [âm nhạc] ngày nay.

segments.viText: Ngựa đã đi xa và dây điện báo đã biến mất, nhưng linh hồn của

segments.viText: thành phố, nguồn năng lượng không ngừng nghỉ đó, vẫn không thay đổi.

segments.text: [music] Thank you for walking through time with me.
segments.viText: [âm nhạc] Cảm ơn bạn đã cùng tôi bước qua thời gian.
